title: Reading a schematic
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: A schematic is a drawing of a circuit. It uses a standard symbol for each part, and lines for the wires.
lines.label: a schematic

lines.caption: It shows exactly how the parts are connected. It does not show how long the wires are, or what the parts look like.
lines.label: connections, not looks

lines.caption: Each symbol is a small sketch. A zigzag is a resistor. Two plates are a capacitor. Two coils side by side are a transformer.
lines.label: one symbol per part

lines.caption: An arrow touching a symbol means the part can be adjusted, like this variable inductor.
lines.label: arrow: adjustable

lines.caption: Small arrows pointing away mean light. A diode with those arrows is a light emitting diode.
lines.label: arrows away: light

lines.caption: The exam shows three small schematics and asks you to name the numbered parts. Now read them yourself.
lines.label: name the parts
